bib.title: Evaluating Object Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 2023 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), pages 292-305

question: Do large vision-language models hallucinate objects absent from the image, and how can this be evaluated more stably than with caption-based CHAIR?
hypothesis: LVLMs are prone to hallucinate objects that appear frequently in the visual instruction data and objects that frequently co-occur with ground-truth objects in the image.
contributions: An empirical study of object hallucination in several representative LVLMs, finding them highly affected.
A discussion of potential reasons, e.g. LVLMs tend to generate frequently appearing or co-occurring objects in the instruction corpora.
POPE, a polling-based hallucination evaluation that is more stable and easily extended to unannotated datasets.

method.summary: Evaluates five open LVLMs on MSCOCO with CHAIR using two caption prompts, analyses hallucinated objects against object frequency and co-occurrence (HR@k), then proposes POPE: yes/no 'Is there a <object> in the image?' questions with 1:1 present/absent objects, absent objects sampled randomly, by popularity or adversarially by co-occurrence. POPE is run on annotation-based and SEEM-segmentation-based object lists.
method.task: object hallucination evaluation of LVLMs (image captioning and yes/no polling)

datasets.name: MSCOCO validation (CHAIR and HR analysis)
datasets.preprocessing: CHAIR considers only the 80 objects of the MSCOCO segmentation challenge

datasets.name: MSCOCO validation (POPE)
datasets.size: 500 images with more than 3 ground-truth objects; 6 questions per image (l = 6)
datasets.preprocessing: Ground-truth objects from annotations; absent objects sampled Random/Popular/Adversarial; ratio of present to absent 1:1

other.Table 7: VE ViT-L/14, AN Attention, LLM LLaMA7B

other.note: CHAIR numbers collected from Dai et al. (2023b); BLIP fine-tuned on VQAv2 from LAVIS used as POPE baseline in Table 11

other.use: parses open-ended VQA answers against 10 reference answers; version not stated

inference.samples: one run per model/setting; random sampling of 500 images; seed not stated
inference.prompting: CHAIR captions: I1 'Generate a short caption of the image.' and I2 'Provide a brief description of the given image.' POPE: 'Is there a/an <object> in the image?'; answer parsed by matching 'Yes'/'No'.

parameters.Popular sampling: top-k most frequent objects in the whole dataset absent from the image, k = l/2
parameters.Adversarial sampling: rank objects by co-occurrence with ground-truth objects, take top-k absent ones, k = l/2

other.prompt_variants_Table4: POPE: 'Is there a <object> in the image?', 'Does the image contain a <object>?', 'Have you noticed a <object> in the image?', 'Can you see a <object> in the image?'; CHAIR: 'Generate a short caption of the image.', 'Provide a brief description of the image.', 'Generate a concise description for the image.', 'Create a short textual summary for the image.'

metrics.name: HR_A@k
metrics.definition: mean over images of Hit@k(i)/Hallucinated(i): share of hallucinated objects that are among the top-k most frequent MSCOCO objects

metrics.name: HR_C@k(o)
metrics.definition: share of hallucinated objects among the top-k objects co-occurring with probing object o

metrics.name: POPE Accuracy / Precision / Recall / F1
metrics.definition: binary classification of Yes/No answers; F1 is the major metric; Precision and Recall are as printed ('ratios of correctly answering questions whose answers are Yes or No')

metrics.name: Yes (%)
metrics.definition: proportion of questions answered Yes, reported for model behaviour

metrics.name: VQA score / accuracy
metrics.definition: VQA score on A-OKVQA, accuracy on GQA, with ChatGPT-assisted answer matching

baselines: BLIP large (CHAIR results from Dai et al. 2023b)
eval.protocol: Single run per setting, no significance tests or seeds reported. Stability tested with 4 prompts each for POPE and CHAIR_I on LLaVA. Consistency check between POPE answers and captions on InstructBLIP and MiniGPT-4.

prompts.text: Generate a short caption of the image.
Provide a brief description of the given image.
Is there a/an <object> in the image?

You are an examiner who can judge whether a student's answer matches the correct answers. Next, I will provide you with 10 correct answers in the form of a list and a student's answer. Please judge whether the student's answer matches one of the 10 correct answers. If it matches, please output the correct answer directly (must be an element in the list, if it matches multiple correct answers, please output the most frequent occurrence in the list); if not, please output <NAN> directly. Do NOT output anything else! correct answers: student answer:

limits: Only object-level hallucination; attributes, counts and positions left for future work.
Measures hallucination only, so a higher POPE score does not mean a stronger model overall.
Evaluated on a subset of each validation set (500 images for POPE) because of compute; results may depend on the sample.
POPE decides Yes/No by word matching; models may not answer with those words.
SEEM labels use the tool's label set, which may diverge from human annotations.
Only a small number of open LVLMs; no closed-source or later models.
The causal link to instruction data is shown by correlation of hallucination counts with frequency, not by retraining on altered data.
Single run, no seeds or confidence intervals reported.

terms.definition: Polling-based Object Probing Evaluation: object hallucination cast as a Yes/No binary classification by prompting LVLMs with questions about probing objects
